editorial.thesis: A healthcare-and-motor-trade city of about 1.3 million. Its retail is heavy on coaching & training and pharmacy & health retail, and thin on grocery & daily needs and restaurants & fast food — and 32% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is about 77% of Delhi's. 14.41 chain outlets per lakh residents against 18.83 in Delhi; 34 of the 51 national brands we track are present, led by Apollo Pharmacy 27, Domino's 23, Café Coffee Day 13.

The mapped economy leans to healthcare. Shares of all mapped places: healthcare 10.7% (Delhi 6.9%); automotive 4.6% (Delhi 3.0%); grocery & daily needs 1.3% (Delhi 2.2%); food & beverage 6.5% (Delhi 8.0%). Raw counts would mislead because Delhi is mapped more completely (87,703 places against 10,835), so we compare mix, not counts.

Supply and demand are misaligned. 5 zones hold 32% of residents with under 60% of the city's average retail depth. Raipur · Kabir Nagar alone has about 102,000 residents and 18 mapped food & drink places.

Retail is more concentrated than in Delhi. 52% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Delhi 47%). The largest cores are Raipur · Ge Road (4,520 places) and Raipur · Devendra Nagar (504).

The widest brand gaps against Delhi. Café Coffee Day 13 outlets vs 145; Domino's 23 outlets vs 140; Apollo Pharmacy 27 outlets vs 108. These are leads to check against live listings, not verdicts: a brand may trade under another name or have opened since the map was updated.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 10 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Delhi, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Raipur · Ge Road and Raipur · Kabir Nagar are the largest zones by residents (588,000 and 102,000). Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 52% of all commercial places, and Raipur · Ge Road alone lists 4,520.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. Raipur · Ge Road holds 108 of the 187 tracked chain outlets, and Raipur · Devendra Nagar adds 13.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. Raipur · Ge Road and Raipur · Mahadev Ghat Road lead on education places (483 and 59, with 205 and 26 coaching centres) — a daytime youth market that residents alone do not show.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. The deepest amber sits in Raipur · Kabir Nagar and Raipur · Mahadev Ghat Road. The blue cores include Raipur · Ge Road.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (87,703 places in Delhi against 10,835 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Delhi; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Delhi, Raipur's mapped places over-index on healthcare (10.7% vs 6.9%), automotive (4.6% vs 3.0%), education (9.9% vs 7.9%) and under-index on grocery & daily needs (1.3% vs 2.2%), food & beverage (6.5% vs 8.0%), desserts & sweets (0.6% vs 0.7%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 187 outlets of 34 tracked national brands within 10 km — 14.41 per lakh residents against Delhi's 18.83 (1289 outlets of 45 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Delhi are Café Coffee Day (13 vs 145); Domino's (23 vs 140); Apollo Pharmacy (27 vs 108). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Delhi's, so low means thin by Delhi's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 10 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Raipur's age mix against Delhi: children (0–14) 29.3% vs 23.1%, 15–24 20.2% vs 20.4%, working age 43.2% vs 49.7%, 60+ 7.4% vs 6.8%. Under-25s are 50% of residents.

zones.492099: An under-served zone: about 102,000 residents, 249 mapped places, 18 food & drink and 3 chain outlets. Depth index 39.
zones.492013: An under-served zone: about 94,000 residents, 278 mapped places, 18 food & drink and 3 chain outlets. Depth index 47.
zones.492003: An under-served zone: about 85,000 residents, 48 mapped places, 1 food & drink and 0 chain outlets. Depth index 9.
zones.492009: Reasonably supplied: 303 places for about 69,000 residents (index 70), 2 chain outlets.
zones.492015: An under-served zone: about 46,000 residents, 125 mapped places, 7 food & drink and 1 chain outlet. Depth index 43.
zones.492014: An under-served zone: about 38,000 residents, 124 mapped places, 11 food & drink and 4 chain outlets. Depth index 52.
zones.492004: A commercial core: 504 mapped places and 13 chain outlets (7% of the city's tracked chains) for about 36,000 residents. A destination zone, so much of its footfall likely lives elsewhere.
zones.492010: A student-and-family belt: 36 education places (14 coaching) and 23 healthcare places for about 36,000 residents, with 22 food & drink places and 3 chain outlets.

zones.492006: Reasonably supplied: 163 places for about 25,000 residents (index 104), 12 chain outlets.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 4.2% of mapped places against 5.7% in Delhi — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Domino's 23 (Delhi 140), KFC 9 (Delhi 51), Pizza Hut 9 (Delhi 68), McDonald's 2 (Delhi 75).
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 2.2% of mapped places against 2.1% in Delhi, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Café Coffee Day 13 (Delhi 145), Starbucks 2 (Delhi 33). No mapped outlet in either city: Chai Sutta Bar.
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 0.6% of mapped places against 0.7% in Delhi — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Baskin Robbins 5 (Delhi 29), Naturals 2 (Delhi 7). No mapped outlet in either city: Cream Stone.
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 1.3% of mapped places against 2.2% in Delhi — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: DMart 8 (Delhi 7), Reliance Smart / Fresh 6 (Delhi 21), Big Bazaar 3 (Delhi 8), Vishal Mega Mart 3 (Delhi 11). No mapped outlet in either city: Star Bazaar.
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 1.4% of mapped places against 1.2% in Delhi — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Apollo Pharmacy 27 (Delhi 108), MedPlus 1 (Delhi 0). No mapped outlet in either city: Wellness Forever, Frank Ross.
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 6.4% of mapped places against 7.0% in Delhi, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Raymond 12 (Delhi 55), Reliance Trends 9 (Delhi 22), Bata 9 (Delhi 66), Tanishq 6 (Delhi 20).
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 8.6% of mapped places against 7.9% in Delhi, so the mix is level.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 3.5% of mapped places against 2.7% in Delhi — above its share.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 4.0% of mapped places against 3.9% in Delhi, so the mix is level.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
